explanations.explanation: Yes. Paul says Christ has set them free for freedom, so the next move is to stand firm and not slide back under slavery again. He is telling them to hold their ground in what Christ has already done for them. (Galatians 5:1)

explanations.answer: Work hard to earn their freedom
explanations.explanation: No, Paul does not put freedom on a workbench and tell them to earn it. He says Christ has already set them free, and then he tells them to stand firm in that freedom. The freedom comes first. (Galatians 5:1)
Not at all. Paul tells them to stand firm, not to hide it or hush it up. The warning is against going back into slavery, not against speaking up about what Christ has done. (Galatians 5:1)
Right. Paul warns them not to be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery. He is saying freedom in Christ is not something they should trade back for bondage. (Galatians 5:1)
No, that warning is right there in the verse. Paul says, "do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery." He is pressing them to stay free in Christ. (Galatians 5:1)

That is what Paul says. If they let themselves be circumcised, then Christ will be of no value to them at all. He is showing how serious it is to turn from Christ to law-keeping as the ground of being right with God. (Galatians 5:2)
No. Paul says the opposite. He says Christ will be of no value to them at all if they let themselves be circumcised in that way. (Galatians 5:2)
Paul does not leave it at the same value. He says Christ will be of no value to them at all if they let themselves be circumcised. That is a strong warning, not a small one. (Galatians 5:2)
No, that is not what Paul says. He says a man who gets himself circumcised is obligated to obey the whole law. One command is not treated like a tiny side dish here. (Galatians 5:3)
Yes, false. Paul says the man is obligated to obey the whole law, not just one command. He is warning them that taking that path means taking on the whole thing. (Galatians 5:3)

explanations.answer: They have been severed from Christ
explanations.explanation: That is Paul’s word. He tells those trying to be justified by the law that they have been severed from Christ. He goes on to say they have fallen away from grace. (Galatians 5:4)

explanations.answer: They have drawn closer to Christ
explanations.explanation: No, Paul says the opposite. He says they have been severed from Christ if they are trying to be justified by the law. That is a serious break, not a closer walk. (Galatians 5:4)
No. Paul says they have fallen away from grace, not piled up extra grace. Trying to be justified by the law cuts them off from Christ instead of adding anything to Him. (Galatians 5:4)

Yes. Paul says, "by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness." He is not talking about earning it by law or effort. Faith is the word that belongs in that blank. (Galatians 5:5)
No, Paul does not say law there. He says they eagerly await through the Spirit by faith. The whole point is trust, not law-keeping as the ground of hope. (Galatians 5:5)
No. Paul says by faith they eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness. Effort is not the word he uses, and it would change the whole feel of the verse. (Galatians 5:5)

That is the one Paul names. He says in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value, and what matters is faith expressing itself through love. He keeps the focus on living faith, not outward markers. (Galatians 5:6)
No, Paul does not say that here. He says what matters is faith expressing itself through love. He is not pointing them to performance as the thing that counts in Christ Jesus. (Galatians 5:6)

explanations.answer: Coming from the right family line
explanations.explanation: No. Paul says neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value in Christ Jesus. What matters is faith expressing itself through love, not family line. (Galatians 5:6)
No, that is not Paul’s point. He says the persuasion does not come from the One who calls them. So the slowing-down voice is not from God. (Galatians 5:8)
Right. Paul says that persuasion does not come from the One who calls them. He is warning them that the pressure they are feeling is not from God. (Galatians 5:8)
That is what Paul says. A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough. One small thing can spread farther than people expect. (Galatians 5:9)
No, Paul does not limit it to the top layer. He says a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough. That is the whole point of the warning. (Galatians 5:9)
No. Paul says it works through the whole batch of dough. He is showing how a little influence can spread through everything. (Galatians 5:9)
Yes. Paul says the one troubling them will bear the judgment, whoever he may be. Paul is confident in the Lord that the truth will stand and the troubler will answer for it. (Galatians 5:10)

explanations.answer: He will be let off free
explanations.explanation: No. Paul says the one troubling them will bear the judgment. He does not shrug it off as if it does not matter. (Galatians 5:10)

explanations.answer: He will be put in charge
explanations.explanation: No, Paul says the troubling one will bear the judgment. That is the opposite of being put in charge. (Galatians 5:10)
No, that is not what Paul is saying. He asks why he is still being persecuted if he is still preaching circumcision. His question shows he is not preaching it. (Galatians 5:11)
Yes, false. Paul’s question makes the point that he is not still preaching circumcision. If he were, he says the offense of the cross would have been abolished. (Galatians 5:11)
Yes. Paul tells the brothers they were called to freedom, and then he warns them not to use that freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Freedom is for serving, not for feeding sin. (Galatians 5:13)
No, Paul does give that warning. He says not to use freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but rather to serve one another in love. He holds freedom and service together. (Galatians 5:13)
That is the decree Paul names. He says the entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: "Love your neighbor as yourself." He is showing how the law’s aim comes together in love. (Galatians 5:14)
No, that is not the one Paul names here. He says the entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: "Love your neighbor as yourself." (Galatians 5:14)
No. Paul names this one: "Love your neighbor as yourself." He says the entire law is fulfilled in that single decree. (Galatians 5:14)
Yes. Paul warns that if they keep on biting and devouring one another, they will be consumed by one another. He is showing where that kind of fighting ends if nobody stops. (Galatians 5:15)
No, Paul does not say scattered here. He says they will be consumed by one another if they keep on biting and devouring one another. That is his warning. (Galatians 5:15)
No. Paul says consumed, not shamed. He is warning them that this kind of conflict will eat them up from the inside. (Galatians 5:15)
